claim: Pseudomonas aeruginosa utilizes the quorum sensing signal 2'-aminoacetophenone (2-AA) to exploit host metabolism and promote immune tolerance.
source: To achieve this, we show that Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA), a recalcitrant pathogen, utilizes the quorum sensing (QS) signal 2'-aminoacetophenone (2-AA).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: 2-AA-driven immune tolerization causes distinct metabolic perturbations in murine macrophages' mitochondrial respiration and bioenergetics.
source: Here, we unveil how 2-AA-driven immune tolerization causes distinct metabolic perturbations in murine macrophages' mitochondrial respiration and bioenergetics.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: 2-AA-mediated metabolic effects stem from decreased pyruvate transport into mitochondria.
source: We present evidence indicating that these effects stem from decreased pyruvate transport into mitochondria.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The reduction in pyruvate transport is attributed to decreased expression of the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (Mpc1).
source: This reduction is attributed to decreased expression of the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (Mpc1), which is mediated by diminished expression and nuclear presence of its transcriptional regulator, estrogen-related nuclear receptor alpha (Esrra).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Decreased Mpc1 expression is mediated by diminished expression and nuclear presence of Esrra.
source: This reduction is attributed to decreased expression of the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (Mpc1), which is mediated by diminished expression and nuclear presence of its transcriptional regulator, estrogen-related nuclear receptor alpha (Esrra).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Esrra exhibits weakened binding to the Mpc1 promoter in 2-AA-tolerized cells.
source: Consequently, Esrra exhibits weakened binding to the Mpc1 promoter.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The weakened Esrra binding to Mpc1 promoter arises from impaired interaction between Esrra and Ppargc1a.
source: This outcome arises from the impaired interaction between Esrra and the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (Ppargc1a).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The cascade of 2-AA effects results in diminished pyruvate influx into mitochondria and reduced ATP production in tolerized murine and human macrophages.
source: Ultimately, this cascade results in diminished pyruvate influx into mitochondria and, consequently reduced ATP production in tolerized murine and human macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Exogenously added ATP in infected macrophages restores the transcript levels of Mpc1 and Esrra.
source: Exogenously added ATP in infected macrophages restores the transcript levels of Mpc1 and Esrra and enhances cytokine production and intracellular bacterial clearance.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Exogenously added ATP enhances cytokine production and intracellular bacterial clearance in infected macrophages.
source: Exogenously added ATP in infected macrophages restores the transcript levels of Mpc1 and Esrra and enhances cytokine production and intracellular bacterial clearance.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Murine infection studies corroborate the 2-AA-mediated long-lasting decrease in ATP and acetyl-CoA.
source: Consistent with the in vitro findings, murine infection studies corroborate the 2-AA-mediated long-lasting decrease in ATP and acetyl-CoA and its association with PA persistence, further supporting this QS signaling molecule as the culprit of the host bioenergetic alterations and PA persistence.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: The 2-AA-mediated decrease in ATP and acetyl-CoA is associated with PA persistence in murine infection studies.
source: Consistent with the in vitro findings, murine infection studies corroborate the 2-AA-mediated long-lasting decrease in ATP and acetyl-CoA and its association with PA persistence, further supporting this QS signaling molecule as the culprit of the host bioenergetic alterations and PA persistence.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Innate immune cells following infection or exposure to microbial products may enter a state of immune tolerance characterized by reduced responsiveness toward microbial re-exposure a few hours later.
source: Studies have shown that innate immune cells following infection or exposure to microbial products may enter a state of immune tolerance characterized by reduced responsiveness toward microbial re-exposure a few hours later (Foster et al., 2007; Bagchi et al., 2007; Masyutina et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Epigenetic and signaling-based mechanisms have been proposed to be involved in host immune tolerance.
source: Epigenetic and signaling-based mechanisms have been proposed to be involved in host immune tolerance (Foster et al., 2007; Bagchi et al., 2007; Masyutina et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Specific metabolic programs are activated in monocytes and macrophages upon exposure to infection and microbial products.
source: It was suggested that specific metabolic programs are activated in monocytes and macrophages upon exposure to infection and microbial products (Tannahill et al., 2013; Galli and Saleh, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Metabolic pathways are essential for generating energy for various cellular functions, including those performed by immune cells.
source: Metabolic pathways are essential for generating energy for various cellular functions, including those performed by immune cells (Wang et al., 2021; Karan et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Macrophages use metabolic pathways to generate energy and metabolites to adapt to changing environments and stimuli.
source: Macrophages use metabolic pathways to generate energy and metabolites to adapt to changing environments and stimuli, thereby enabling them to cope with the needs of a fluctuating immune response (Galli and Saleh, 2020; Bird, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a recalcitrant ESKAPE pathogen that causes acute and persistent infections.
source: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA), a recalcitrant ESKAPE (Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, PA, and Enterobacter sp.) pathogen that causes acute and persistent infections, secretes virulence-associated low molecular weight signaling molecules, several of which are regulated by quorum sensing (QS) (Déziel et al., 2005; Xiao et al., 2006; Eickhoff and Bassler, 2018; Fuqua and Greenberg, 2002) and able to modulate host immune responses (Kariminik et al., 2017; Liu et al., 2015; Bandyopadhaya et al., 2012; Bandyopadhaya et al., 2016b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Pseudomonas aeruginosa secretes virulence-associated low molecular weight signaling molecules regulated by quorum sensing.
source: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA), a recalcitrant ESKAPE (Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, PA, and Enterobacter sp.) pathogen that causes acute and persistent infections, secretes virulence-associated low molecular weight signaling molecules, several of which are regulated by quorum sensing (QS) (Déziel et al., 2005; Xiao et al., 2006; Eickhoff and Bassler, 2018; Fuqua and Greenberg, 2002) and able to modulate host immune responses (Kariminik et al., 2017; Liu et al., 2015; Bandyopadhaya et al., 2012; Bandyopadhaya et al., 2016b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Quorum sensing is a cell density-dependent signaling system bacteria use to synchronize their activities.
source: QS is a cell density-dependent signaling system bacteria used to synchronize their activities (Déziel et al., 2005; Xiao et al., 2006; Eickhoff and Bassler, 2018; Fuqua and Greenberg, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: MvfR (a.k.a. PqsR), a critical QS transcription factor of PA, regulates the synthesis of many small molecules, including 2-AA.
source: MvfR (a.k.a. PqsR), a critical QS transcription factor of PA, regulates the synthesis of many small molecules, including signaling molecules such as 2'-aminoacetophenone (2-AA) (Déziel et al., 2005; Cao et al., 2001; Déziel et al., 2004; Kesarwani et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In vivo studies have demonstrated that 2-AA enables PA to persist in infected murine tissues by promoting innate immune tolerance through HDAC1-mediated epigenetic reprogramming.
source: In vivo studies have demonstrated that 2-AA enables PA to persist in infected murine tissues by promoting innate immune tolerance through histone deacetylase 1 (HDAC1)-mediated epigenetic reprogramming (Bandyopadhaya et al., 2012; Bandyopadhaya et al., 2016b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: 2-AA tolerization reprograms the host inflammatory signaling cascade by maintaining chromatin in a 'silent' state through increased HDAC1 expression and activity and decreased HAT activity.
source: 2-AA tolerization reprograms the host inflammatory signaling cascade by maintaining chromatin in a 'silent' state through increased HDAC1 expression and activity and decreased histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity (Bandyopadhaya et al., 2016b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: 2-AA tolerization impacts the protein-protein interaction between HAT and cyclic AMP response element-binding protein/HDAC1 and p50/p65 nuclear factor-κB subunits.
source: These changes also impact the protein-protein interaction between HAT and cyclic AMP response element-binding protein/HDAC1 and p50/p65 nuclear factor-κB subunits (Bandyopadhaya et al., 2016b; Bandyopadhaya et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: The 2-AA-mediated tolerization permits PA to persist in infected tissues.
source: The 2-AA-mediated tolerization permits PA to persist in infected tissues (Bandyopadhaya et al., 2012; Bandyopadhaya et al., 2016b), underscoring the difference from lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-mediated tolerization, which instead leads to bacterial clearance and involves different HDACs (Wheeler et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: LPS-mediated tolerization leads to bacterial clearance and involves different HDACs than 2-AA tolerization.
source: The 2-AA-mediated tolerization permits PA to persist in infected tissues (Bandyopadhaya et al., 2012; Bandyopadhaya et al., 2016b), underscoring the difference from lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-mediated tolerization, which instead leads to bacterial clearance and involves different HDACs (Wheeler et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mitochondria are crucial for the regulation, differentiation, and survival of macrophages and other immune cells.
source: Mitochondria, the 'powerhouse' of the cells, are crucial for the regulation, differentiation, and survival of macrophages and other immune cells (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Previous in vivo and in vitro studies indicated that 2-AA affects metabolic functions in skeletal muscle.
source: Our group's previous in vivo and in vitro studies indicated that 2-AA affects metabolic functions in skeletal muscle, which contains a high concentration of mitochondria (Tzika et al., 2013; Bandyopadhaya et al., 2016a; Chakraborty et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: Injection of 2-AA in murine skeletal muscle dampens the expression of genes associated with OXPHOS and Ppargc1b.
source: Injection of 2-AA in murine skeletal muscle dampens the expression of genes associated with OXPHOS and the master regulator of mitochondrial biogenesis peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ coactivator-1 beta (Ppargc1b) (Tzika et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: Another PA QS molecule, 3-oxo-C12-HSL, attenuates the expression of Ppargc1a.
source: Another PA QS molecule, 3-oxo-C12-HSL, attenuates the expression of Ppargc1a (Maurice et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ppargc1a and Ppargc1b belong to the PPARγ family of inducible transcriptional coactivators and are known regulators of mitochondrial metabolism.
source: Ppargc1a and Ppargc1b belong to the PPARγ family of inducible transcriptional coactivators and are known regulators of mitochondrial metabolism (Lelliott and Vidal-Puig, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The coactivator Ppargc1 proteins are involved in various cellular energy metabolic processes.
source: The coactivator Ppargc1 proteins are involved in various cellular energy metabolic processes (Supruniuk et al., 2017; Coppi et al., 2021), including but not limited to mitochondrial metabolism (Lin et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Esrra plays a role in coordinating metabolic capacity with energy demand in health and disease.
source: Recent studies have also emphasized the role of estrogen-related nuclear receptor α (Esrra) in coordinating metabolic capacity with energy demand in health and disease (Huss et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ppargc1a activates Esrra transcriptional activity through protein-protein interaction, which enhances the expression of Esrra.
source: Ppargc1a activates Esrra transcriptional activity through protein-protein interaction, which enhances the expression of Esrra (Schreiber et al., 2003; Laganière et al., 2004) and other mitochondrial genes involved in lipid metabolism and OXPHOS (Villena, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ppargc1a/Esrra axis has been extensively studied in cancer and established as a central regulatory node of energy metabolism that induces the global expression of genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis and functions.
source: Ppargc1a/Esrra axis has been extensively studied in cancer and established as a central regulatory node of energy metabolism that induces the global expression of genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis and functions (Ranhotra, 2010; Deblois and Giguère, 2011; Ranhotra, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Esrra has been shown to occupy the promoter regions of many genes participating in the TCA cycle and OXPHOS, including Mpc1.
source: Esrra has been shown to occupy the promoter regions of many genes participating in the TCA cycle and OXPHOS (Charest-Marcotte et al., 2010; Eichner and Giguère, 2011), including the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (Mpc1).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In human renal carcinoma cells, Ppargc1a/Esrra interaction results in efficient activation of Mpc1 expression and transport of pyruvate into mitochondrion for efficient OXPHOS and energy production.
source: In human renal carcinoma cells, Ppargc1a/Esrra interaction results in efficient activation of Mpc1 expression and transport of pyruvate into mitochondrion for efficient OXPHOS and energy production (Koh et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Following the first 2-AA exposure, a significant increase in the concentrations of intracellular ATP was observed in BMDM cells exposed to 2-AA for 1 and 6 hr compared to their corresponding naïve control cells.
source: Initially, following the first 2-AA exposure (black bars), a significant increase in the concentrations of intracellular ATP (Figure 1B) and acetyl-CoA (Figure 1C) was observed in BMDM cells exposed to 2-AA for 1 and 6 hr compared to their corresponding naïve control cells (gray bars).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Following the first 2-AA exposure, a significant increase in the concentrations of acetyl-CoA was observed in BMDM cells exposed to 2-AA for 1 and 6 hr compared to their corresponding naïve control cells.
source: Initially, following the first 2-AA exposure (black bars), a significant increase in the concentrations of intracellular ATP (Figure 1B) and acetyl-CoA (Figure 1C) was observed in BMDM cells exposed to 2-AA for 1 and 6 hr compared to their corresponding naïve control cells (gray bars).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cells exposed to 2-AA for 48 hr appeared to have entered a state of tolerance as ATP and acetyl-CoA levels were decreased compared to 2-AA exposures for a shorter time.
source: However, cells exposed to 2-AA for 48 hr (black bar) appeared to have entered a state of tolerance as ATP and acetyl-CoA levels were decreased compared to 2-AA exposures for a shorter time (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: BMDM cells showed unresponsiveness to 2-AA re-exposure as evidenced by the similar levels of ATP and acetyl-CoA compared to cells exposed to 2-AA for 48 hr.
source: Figure 1B and C (red bars) shows the unresponsiveness of BMDM cells to 2-AA re-exposure as evidenced by the similar levels of ATP and acetyl-CoA compared to cells exposed to 2-AA for 48 hr (first exposure black bars).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: The sustained unresponsiveness of the cells to re-exposure indicates that the cells exhibited innate immunological memory, which could not be reverted by 2-AA re-exposure.
source: The sustained unresponsiveness of the cells to re-exposure indicates that the cells exhibited innate immunological memory, which could not be reverted by 2-AA re-exposure.
evidence: This is stated in the text as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Similar responsiveness patterns of ATP and acetyl-CoA as with BMDM cells were observed in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells following exposure or re-exposure to 2-AA.
source: Similar responsiveness patterns of ATP and acetyl-CoA as with BMDM cells were observed in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) or human monocyte THP-1 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) following exposure or re-exposure to 2-AA.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Similar responsiveness patterns of ATP and acetyl-CoA as with BMDM cells were observed in human monocyte THP-1 cells following exposure or re-exposure to 2-AA.
source: Similar responsiveness patterns of ATP and acetyl-CoA as with BMDM cells were observed in murine macrophage RAW 264.7 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) or human monocyte THP-1 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) following exposure or re-exposure to 2-AA.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 2-AA impacts crucial energy metabolites in macrophages.
source: These results reinforce the notion that 2-AA impacts crucial energy metabolites in macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: 2-AA tolerization arrests macrophages in a sustained 2-AA-unresponsive state.
source: These findings confirm that 2-AA mediates energy homeostatic and metabolic alterations in the immune cells and that 2-AA tolerization arrests these cells in a sustained 2-AA-unresponsive state.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: LPS re-exposure of the 2-AA-tolerized BMDM cells did not significantly increase ATP levels.
source: LPS re-exposure of the 2-AA-tolerized BMDM cells did not significantly (p=0.9) increase ATP levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), indicating that 2-AA cross-tolerized the cells to this heterologous bacterial immunostimulant.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: 2-AA cross-tolerized BMDM cells to LPS, a heterologous bacterial immunostimulant.
source: LPS re-exposure of the 2-AA-tolerized BMDM cells did not significantly (p=0.9) increase ATP levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), indicating that 2-AA cross-tolerized the cells to this heterologous bacterial immunostimulant.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Increased ATP levels were observed following LPS stimulation of the non-tolerized BMDM cells.
source: On the other hand, as expected, we observed increased ATP levels following LPS stimulation of the non-tolerized BMDM cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The broad spectrum of 2-AA cross-tolerization strongly suggests an interplay of epigenetic mechanism rather than ligand-receptor-mediated signaling-based mechanism.
source: The broad spectrum of 2-AA cross-tolerization strongly suggests an interplay of epigenetic mechanism rather than ligand-receptor-mediated signaling-based mechanism in bringing out the observed 2-AA-mediated tolerance.
evidence: This is stated in the text as an interpretation of the data.

claim: 1 hr 2-AA exposure of naïve cells significantly increased OCR compared to naïve control cells.
source: Values of basal (Figure 1E) and maximal (Figure 1F) mitochondrial respiration and spare respiratory capacity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) interpreted from these measurements revealed that 1 hr 2-AA exposure of naïve cells significantly increased OCR compared to naïve control cells.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figures 1E, 1F, and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: At 24 hr post-2-AA exposure, cells had a significantly reduced basal OCR level than the control BMDM cells, indicating decreased OXPHOS and an overall quiescent phenotype of tolerized macrophages.
source: At 24 hr post-2-AA exposure, cells had a significantly reduced basal OCR level than the control BMDM cells, indicating decreased OXPHOS and an overall quiescent phenotype of tolerized macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: Re-exposure of tolerized macrophages with 2-AA did not augment maximal and basal OCR, indicating the unresponsiveness of tolerized BMDM cells.
source: Re-exposure of tolerized macrophages with 2-AA also did not augment maximal and basal OCR (Figure 1D–F), indicating the unresponsiveness of tolerized BMDM cells.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figures 1D-F.

claim: Ultramicroscopic examination of RAW 264.7 cells exposed to 2-AA for 48 hr shows the same number of mitochondria as in control cells, but their mitochondrial morphology is altered, appearing smaller and round and having reduced cristae indicating dysfunctional mitochondria.
source: Ultramicroscopic examination of RAW 264.7 cells exposed to 2-AA for 48 hr although shows the same number of mitochondria as in control cells, their mitochondrial morphology is altered, appearing smaller and round and having reduced cristae indicating dysfunctional mitochondria (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: 2-AA tolerization induces a quiescent phenotype in macrophages characterized by defective OXPHOS.
source: These OCR data are consistent with the previous direct measurements of ATP (Figure 1B) and acetyl-CoA (Figure 1C) and support the notion that 2-AA tolerization induces a quiescent phenotype in these cells characterized by defective OXPHOS.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: 2-AA mediates energy homeostatic and metabolic alterations in the immune cells.
source: These findings confirm that 2-AA mediates energy homeostatic and metabolic alterations in the immune cells and that 2-AA tolerization arrests these cells in a sustained 2-AA-unresponsive state.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: RAW 264.7 cells initially exposed to 2-AA for 1 or 3 hr exhibited significantly higher concentrations of cytosolic and mitochondrial pyruvate compared to the corresponding naïve control cells.
source: RAW 264.7 cells initially exposed to 2-AA for 1 or 3 hr (black bars) exhibited significantly higher concentrations of cytosolic and mitochondrial pyruvate compared to the corresponding naïve control cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Pyruvate significantly decreased over time in cytosolic and mitochondrial fractions as cells were entering into the tolerized state.
source: Pyruvate significantly decreased over time in cytosolic and mitochondrial fractions as cells were entering into the tolerized state (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Tolerized cells remain unresponsive to 2-AA re-exposure, exhibiting no significant change in the concentration of pyruvate in the cytosolic or mitochondrial fraction.
source: Tolerized cells remain unresponsive to 2-AA re-exposure (red bars), exhibiting no significant change in the concentration of pyruvate in the cytosolic or mitochondrial fraction (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Western blot studies of whole-cell lysates of RAW 246.7 cells exposed to 2-AA showed a significant decrease over time in the abundance of Mpc1 protein.
source: Western blot studies of whole-cell lysates of RAW 246.7 cells exposed to 2-AA showed a significant decrease over time in the abundance of Mpc1 protein, and tolerized cells remain unresponsive to 2-AA re-exposure (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Tolerized cells remain unresponsive to 2-AA re-exposure with respect to Mpc1 protein levels.
source: Western blot studies of whole-cell lysates of RAW 246.7 cells exposed to 2-AA showed a significant decrease over time in the abundance of Mpc1 protein, and tolerized cells remain unresponsive to 2-AA re-exposure (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 2-AA tolerization dysregulates Mpc1-mediated transport of the pyruvate into mitochondria.
source: Together, these findings suggest that 2-AA tolerization dysregulates Mpc1-mediated transport of the pyruvate into mitochondria.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Western blot studies of whole-cell lysates showed a significant decrease over time in the abundance of Esrra protein following first exposure of RAW 246.7 cells to 2-AA.
source: Western blot studies of whole-cell lysates showed a significant decrease over time in the abundance of Esrra protein following first exposure of RAW 246.7 cells to 2-AA, while tolerized cells remain unresponsive to 2-AA re-exposure (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Tolerized cells remain unresponsive to 2-AA re-exposure with respect to Esrra protein levels.
source: Western blot studies of whole-cell lysates showed a significant decrease over time in the abundance of Esrra protein following first exposure of RAW 246.7 cells to 2-AA, while tolerized cells remain unresponsive to 2-AA re-exposure (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Both cytosolic and nuclear fractions had lower levels of Esrra protein in tolerized cells than their corresponding control cells.
source: By assessing the cytosolic and nuclear abundance of Esrra in tolerized cells, we found that both fractions had lower levels of Esrra protein than their corresponding control cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: An Esrra-binding putative DNA motif (TNAAGGTCA) has been identified upstream of the Mpc1 promoter in humans.
source: Furthermore, because an Esrra-binding putative DNA motif (TNAAGGTCA) has been identified upstream of the Mpc1 promoter in humans (Koh et al., 2018), and we found the same motif to be present 1.5 kB upstream of the transcription start site of mouse Mpc1 promoter, we analyzed if tolerization led to reduced Esrra binding to the Mpc1 promoter motif TNAAGGTCA.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and the authors' own findings.

claim: The same Esrra-binding motif (TNAAGGTCA) is present 1.5 kB upstream of the transcription start site of mouse Mpc1 promoter.
source: Furthermore, because an Esrra-binding putative DNA motif (TNAAGGTCA) has been identified upstream of the Mpc1 promoter in humans (Koh et al., 2018), and we found the same motif to be present 1.5 kB upstream of the transcription start site of mouse Mpc1 promoter, we analyzed if tolerization led to reduced Esrra binding to the Mpc1 promoter motif TNAAGGTCA.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a finding by the authors.

claim: In tolerized cells, Esrra binds approximately fourfold less efficiently to the putative binding site on the Mpc1 than in corresponding control cells.
source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay followed by qPCR analysis revealed that in tolerized cells, Esrra binds approximately fourfold less efficiently to the putative binding site on the Mpc1 than in corresponding control cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Less Esrra was detected when Ppargc1a was pulled down in the presence of 2-AA than in naïve control cells.
source: As shown in Figure 3D less Esrra was detected when Ppargc1a was pulled down in the presence of 2-AA than in naïve control cells.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Reverse co-IP with Esrra protein showed lower levels of Ppargc1a in the presence of 2-AA than in naïve control cells.
source: Moreover, reverse co-IP with Esrra protein showed lower levels of Ppargc1a in the presence of 2-AA than in naïve control cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: In the tolerized macrophages, Ppargc1a/Esrra interaction is impaired.
source: These results indicate that in the tolerized macrophages, Ppargc1a/Esrra interaction is impaired (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: RAW 264.7 cells infected with PA14 showed lower RNA transcript levels of Mpc1 compared to ΔmvfR.
source: Using RAW 264.7 cells infected with the wild-type PA strain PA14 or isogenic ΔmvfR mutant, which does not produce 2-AA (Kesarwani et al., 2011) we observed lower RNA transcript levels of Mpc1 (Figure 4A), Esrra (Figure 4B), and Ppargc1a (Figure 4C) in PA14 compared to ΔmvfR.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: RAW 264.7 cells infected with PA14 showed lower RNA transcript levels of Esrra compared to ΔmvfR.
source: Using RAW 264.7 cells infected with the wild-type PA strain PA14 or isogenic ΔmvfR mutant, which does not produce 2-AA (Kesarwani et al., 2011) we observed lower RNA transcript levels of Mpc1 (Figure 4A), Esrra (Figure 4B), and Ppargc1a (Figure 4C) in PA14 compared to ΔmvfR.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: RAW 264.7 cells infected with PA14 showed lower RNA transcript levels of Ppargc1a compared to ΔmvfR.
source: Using RAW 264.7 cells infected with the wild-type PA strain PA14 or isogenic ΔmvfR mutant, which does not produce 2-AA (Kesarwani et al., 2011) we observed lower RNA transcript levels of Mpc1 (Figure 4A), Esrra (Figure 4B), and Ppargc1a (Figure 4C) in PA14 compared to ΔmvfR.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The addition of 2-AA to ΔmvfR decreased the levels of Mpc1, Esrra, and Ppargc1a gene transcripts to levels similar to the PA14 infection condition.
source: The addition of 2-AA to ΔmvfR decreased the levels of these gene transcripts to levels similar to the PA14 infection condition, supporting the role of 2-AA in effect.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figures 4A-C.

claim: The addition of ATP in PA14-infected cells elevated the transcript levels of Esrra, Mpc1, and Ppargc1a, reaching levels similar to those observed in ΔmvfR infected macrophages.
source: The findings indicate that the addition of ATP in PA14-infected cells elevated the transcript levels of Esrra, Mpc1, and Ppargc1a, reaching levels similar to those observed in ΔmvfR infected macrophages (Figure 4A, B, and C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figures 4A-C.

claim: Reduced Mpc1 function is due to 2-AA tolerization on the transcriptional activation of Mpc1 through the Ppargc1a/Esrra axis.
source: These results indicate that reduced Mpc1 function is due to 2-AA tolerization on the transcriptional activation of Mpc1 through the Ppargc1a/Esrra axis.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Macrophages infected with PA14 showed increased bacterial burden than the cells infected with ΔmvfR.
